Subject: Region binding requirements for EU PII - DPA questions

Laura —

Thanks for the demo last week. Two quick things our DPO wants clarified before we proceed to procurement:

1) Can Redwood commit that EU customer data (PII + patient metadata) will be processed and stored only in EU-hosted infrastructure under the standard hosted plan? Is there an explicit geographic anchor or is it affinity-based?

2) If there is a capacity or regional outage, what are your transient cross-region processing windows (hours) and what telemetry/notifications do you provide to customers?

3) Please share the current subprocessor roster and explain how you notify customers of additions/changes.

4) Our legal team will likely redline the DPA. Any constraints we should expect for location or KMS-related clauses?

I attached our short questionnaire (orchid_compliance_questionnaire.pdf). Can you confirm whether a KMS in EU with customer-managed keys is an option for Hosted customers vs Dedicated/Private?

Appreciate a short written response so I can loop in procurement. If faster, we can take a 30-min call next week.

— Sarah
Sarah Owens
Head of Security & Privacy
Orchid Health

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Region binding requirements for EU PII - DPA questions

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — this is straightforward to address up front. Summary answers below; I also attached: Redwood_DPA_v3.2.pdf, the May subprocessor roster, and a schematic of our routing/anchor model (geo-routing-diagram.png).

1) Location-anchor model: we offer an EU location-anchor option that gives EU affinity for all processing/storage. For Hosted customers this is an "affinity + guarded-failover" configuration: we route to EU pools by default and we will not place standing replicas outside the region. We do allow transient, conditional cross-region processing only in operational emergencies or when capacity constraints would otherwise cause customer outages.

2) Transient windows & notification: our emergency transient window is contractually capped to 48 hours for customer-facing workloads; any cross-region processing beyond 48 hours requires advance approval and triggers either an escrow/KMS handoff or a migration plan. For transparency we provide:
  - real-time incident notification (email + console banner) when an outbound hop occurs
  - per-request telemetry (timestamps + region_of_processing tag) available in the Console and in a downloadable audit log

3) Subprocessors: current roster attached (subprocessor_roster_may2025.csv). We notify customers 30 days prior to major additions and provide an opt-out path for certain categories under the DPA addendum.

4) KMS and DPA notes: customer-managed keys in-region are currently available for Private deployments. For Dedicated we can offer split-key arrangements and regionally scoped key material in some contracts. For Hosted customers we can offer an HSM-backed key store with geobinding controls as an addendum (not standard).

Next steps I recommend: 1) 30-min call with our procurement and privacy lead to walk the DPA addendum language; 2) we send a proposed location-anchor DPA addendum for your legal review; 3) ops will prepare a short evidence package (telemetry export + recent incident runbook excerpt).

Do any of those steps look good? I can propose times.

Best,

• Can you confirm the precise notification SLA (e.g., within 60 minutes of a transient hop being triggered)?
• We need to see the subprocessor roster in a machine-readable CSV (I opened the attachment but legal asked for a canonical feed URL).

Sarah —

Thanks, and those are fair asks. Quick commitments and answers so your GC has something concrete: 

• Notification SLA: we will commit to 60 minutes initial notification to the configured DPO/technical contacts (email + console alert) for any outbound hop. Full audit export available within 24 hours.

• Subprocessor roster feed: we published a canonical CSV at https://redwood.company/docs/subprocessors/may-2025 (link included above). The attached CSV is a snapshot; Ops will include an export API contract reference in the evidence package.

• KMS/BYOK: for Hosted customers we do not expose BYOK today as a standard option. That said, we can offer an HSM-escrow arrangement scoped to the location-anchor addendum (requires an enterprise contract). For low-friction next steps, we typically propose Dedicated with a regional key split as the baseline for PHI. We will include language in the addendum that narrows redlines to the location + KMS sections only.

Proposed next steps:
1) Book the 30-min sync on Wed 14 May 10:30 PT (I’ll send an invite).
2) We’ll circulate a targeted DPA addendum draft within 48 hours after the call to your GC and legal@orchidhealth.com.
3) Ops will bundle a telemetry export + runbook excerpt and a DocuSign-ready addendum.

If that sounds good I’ll lock the time and route a brief agenda.

Best,
